```sql
-- name: audit_log_page
-- owner: compliance
-- params: tenant_id, table_name, row_id, from, to, limit, offset
-- One page of the audit trail, newest first. table_name and row_id are
-- optional; pass NULL to skip the filter.
SELECT a.id,
       a.tenant_id,
       a.table_name,
       a.row_id,
       a.action,
       a.old_data,
       a.new_data,
       a.actor_id,
       a.is_system,
       a.created_at
  FROM audit_log a
 WHERE a.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
   AND (%(table_name)s::text IS NULL OR a.table_name = %(table_name)s)
   AND (%(row_id)s::uuid IS NULL OR a.row_id = %(row_id)s)
   AND a.created_at >= %(from)s
   AND a.created_at <  %(to)s
 ORDER BY a.created_at DESC, a.id DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s OFFSET %(offset)s
```

Ik geef de query ongewijzigd terug. De parameters worden client-side als constanten ingevuld, waardoor de planner de `IS NULL OR`-takken al wegvouwt en `audit_log_tenant_created_at_idx` (tenant_id, created_at) backward kan scannen met een incremental sort op `id`. Echte winst vereist een index op (tenant_id, created_at DESC, id DESC) of keyset-paginering in plaats van OFFSET, maar beide vallen buiten de regels (schemawijziging respectievelijk andere parameters).
